subject: Pricing ownership & next steps — PayRoute pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@payroute.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@payroute.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing ownership & next steps — PayRoute pilot
Attachments: Redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the walkthrough of PayRoute's planned conversational flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on economics and decision owners: 

Summary of ask
- Expected token volumes: ~200M tokens / month (spike to 300M in promo months)
- Desired pilot: 3 months, targeted to instrument search + customer messaging flows
- Initial budget range you mentioned on the call: $150k–$250k for the pilot period (we'll break down run rate)

Immediate questions for your team
1) Who will be the economic buyer that signs the contract? (Name & title)
2) Who in Finance needs to sign off on pricing/PO — and do they have a standard procurement form?
3) Any mandatory security artifacts (SOC2, SLA, data retention) beyond what we shared?

What we will deliver by Wednesday EOD
- A short pricing sheet with unit economics (tokens -> $) and a 1M-token reference price for committed volumes (attached draft)
- A draft SOW for the 3-month pilot for your legal and procurement teams
- Suggested mutual action plan with milestones and dates

If you can confirm the econ buyer & finance approver, we will incorporate their names into the SOW and send a procurement-ready packet.

Thanks — cc'ing Sean (pricing lead) and Monica (CS) to track delivery.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@payroute.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@payroute.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ownership & next steps — PayRoute pilot
Attachments: PayRoute_RFP_Form.pdf

Thanks Camila — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: yes, 200M tokens/month is our baseline; during marketing pushes we could hit 300M for 4–6 weeks.
- Budget: for a pilot we are thinking in the $150k–$250k band you captured. That would need to cover usage + any implementation assistance.

Answers to your questions:
1) Economic buyer is Evan Morris, CFO (will introduce).
2) Finance approver for procurement is Leah Ortiz (Sr. Manager, Finance) — she owns PO flow and vendor onboarding. I attached our procurement form (procurement does like vendor-level docs).
3) Security: SOC2 Type II + an IP/data segregation note should do for now; procurement may request specific clauses.

Can you send the pricing sheet and a draft SOW? If you can also include a clear $/1M token reference (and what volume tiers reduce that), it will help Leah evaluate.

I will introduce Evan and Leah on a follow-up thread once I confirm their availability.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product Partnerships | PayRoute
alyssa.chen@payroute.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ownership & next steps — PayRoute pilot
Attachments: pricing-breakdown-1M.xlsx

Camila — quick internal note on pricing posture for PayRoute: 

- Target reference price: $1,200 / 1M tokens at committed monthly volume >=150M tokens.
- Spike protection: we should propose an overage band (e.g., 25% above committed at a +20% marginal rate) to keep cost predictable.
- Pilot discount: recommend a pilot rate that is roughly 10–15% off committed list to make the initial PO frictionless — still protect us with minimum monthly commit (e.g., 100M tokens).

Ask: Can you confirm whether PayRoute expects upfront prepay for the pilot or net-30 PO billing? If they need to stay within $150k–$250k, map those numbers to both prepay and monthly billing variants.

I'll attach a quick unit-econ spreadsheet (token tiers, expected monthly USD at each tier) so we can include an explicit $/1M table in the packet. Priya — please review SOW boilerplate for data retention clause and highlight any changes that procurement typically asks for.

Sean
Director, Pricing & GTM Economics | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@payroute.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@payroute.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ownership & next steps — PayRoute pilot
Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf, Redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Alyssa / Tom — thanks, adding the packet as discussed. Attached: a) draft SOW for a 3-month pilot, b) pricing sheet with $/1M reference and tiered discounts, c) brief mutual action plan. Highlights below: 

Packet highlights
- Reference price (committed >=150M/mo): $1,200 / 1M tokens. Pilot pricing proposal: $1,050 / 1M tokens for the 3-month pilot with a 100M monthly minimum.
- Example math: if PayRoute runs 200M tokens in a month at pilot pricing -> billed amount = (200 / 1) * $1,050 = $210,000 for that month (we note spike protection rules).
- Billing options: (A) Prepay for pilot (single invoice), (B) Net-30 monthly invoicing with PO + vendor onboarding. Both options listed in section 3 of the SOW.
- Security & procurement: SOC2 Type II report included; Priya has flagged a short data-retention clause for legal review.

Requested next steps
1) Alyssa: introduce Evan (CFO) and Leah (Finance approver) on this thread so we can share the packet and answer their procurement questions.
2) PayRoute: confirm preferred billing flow (prepay vs PO) and whether the $150k–$250k is per-month or total pilot budget.
3) Redwood: Sean will prepare the final unit-econ table; Priya will circulate the small edits to the SOW for procurement.

If you want, we can schedule a 20-minute call with Evan & Leah to walk through the packet next week.

Thanks,
Camila

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@payroute.com>

Camila / Sean — this is great, thank you. I will: 
- Introduce Evan (CFO) and Leah (Finance) on Monday morning.
- Confirm our preference — likely net-30 PO for procurement reasons, but I will verify whether a single prepay would be easier for the pilot.
- Send your packet to procurement and follow up with any questions; Leah will want to see the explicit $/1M table and the procurement form I attached earlier.

Also: Evan will want a quick call — please propose a few 20-minute windows for next week and we will pick one.

Talk Monday.
—Alyssa
